terms.description:
Terms acceptance evidence.

Non-Reliance partners use hosted TOS signing and send
`terms.signed_agreement_id`. Reliance partners collect acceptance in
their own UI and send `terms.accepted_at` with optional acceptance
metadata.

signed_agreement_id.description:
Signed agreement ID obtained from the hosted TOS signing flow.

**Required** for non-Reliance partners. **Optional** for Reliance
partners — Reliance partners may instead send `accepted_at`
(mutually exclusive). Exactly one of `signed_agreement_id` or
`accepted_at` must be present when the partner is Reliance.

Obtained via `POST /v1/individuals/tos/sessions` then user signing.
Each `signed_agreement_id` is **single-use** — it can only be used
for one application. Re-using a consumed ID returns `404 Session
not found`. Create a new TOS session for each new application.

accepted_at.description:
Reliance partner only: timestamp of partner-collected TOS
acceptance. Use ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 in UTC. Mutually exclusive
with `signed_agreement_id`. Must not be in the future.

Partners with partner-attested TOS timestamps enabled may collect TOS
acceptance in their own UI and submit the timestamp here, bypassing
the hosted signing flow. Other partners MUST NOT send this field —
doing so returns 400.

acceptance_ip.description:
End-user IP captured by the partner at TOS acceptance. Recorded
alongside `accepted_at` as evidence. **Only accepted when
`accepted_at` is present** — sending this field on the hosted
(`signed_agreement_id`) path returns 400.

acceptance_user_agent.description:
End-user User-Agent header captured by the partner at TOS
acceptance. Recorded alongside `accepted_at` as evidence.
**Only accepted when `accepted_at` is present** — sending this
field on the hosted (`signed_agreement_id`) path returns 400.

email.description: Email address. Must be a valid email format. Max 255 characters.

calling_code.description: Phone calling code. 2–4 characters. Must start with `+` followed by 1–3 digits (e.g., `+1`, `+44`, `+86`).

number.description: Phone number without country code. 1–30 characters, digits only (e.g., `4155551234`).

date_of_birth.description: Date of birth in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Applicant must be at least 18 years old.

nationality.description:
Nationality in ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 format (e.g. `US`, `BR`, `GB`).

Any valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code is accepted. Nationality
is NOT restricted to the operating-country allowlist. If nationality
is on the prohibited list (OFAC-sanctioned), the application is
routed through Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) rather than rejected
synchronously. Nationalities whose risk rating is not yet configured
are also routed through EDD with a warn-level operational signal.
(Compliance rule 2026-05-23.)

tax_residence_country.description:
Tax residence country in ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 format (e.g. `US`, `BR`, `MX`).

This is the country where the applicant pays taxes. It is sent with
`tin` to Sumsub as `fixedInfo.taxResidenceCountry` and is used by
downstream vendor adapters when they require country-specific routing.
It does not need to match `residential_address.country`,
`document.country`, or `person.nationality`.

tin.description:
Individual taxpayer identification number for the customer's tax residence country.

New integrations should send this field instead of the legacy
top-level `identity` object. The server stores it internally as a
generic `tax_id`; vendor adapters may derive country-specific handling
from `tax_residence_country` when needed.

state.description:
State or province code. 1–64 characters.

**For US addresses (`country = "US"`)**, the value MUST be a 2-letter
ISO 3166-2 US state code (50 states + DC, e.g. `CA`, `TX`, `WA`,
`DC`). Free-form values are rejected with
`00010057 invalid_us_state_code`.
US territories (PR, GU, VI, AS, MP) are not currently accepted.
A small subset of states is not supported for retail KYC residency
(license-driven blocklist — currently `HI, NY, TN`); supplying
one of these returns `00010058 state_not_supported_for_kyc`.
All other 50-state-plus-DC codes (`CA`, `TX`, `WA`, `DC`, …) are
accepted.

For non-US addresses, any plain text value within 1–64 characters is
accepted.

individual_applications.create.description:
Initiate Individual Application

Create a new individual KYC application in `DRAFT`.

Send the required KYC2 profile groups: `terms`, `contact`, `person`, `residential_address`, and `document`. The response returns `customer_id`, `external_customer_id`, status fields, and `pending_documents`.

After creation, upload the required KYC2 documents and call `POST /v1/individuals/applications/{customer_id}/submit` to start asynchronous verification. EDD/Tier3 data is not accepted at creation; provide it later via `PATCH /applications/{customer_id}` and `POST /upgrade` when needed.

`Idempotency-Key` is required. Replay compares `(eid, idempotency_key, contact.email)` and returns the original response when it matches.

For the full flow, TOS options, document requirements, country rules, webhooks, and EDD upgrade path, see the [Individual Onboarding Overview](https://developer.1money.com/reference/individual_onboarding_overview).

Upload Application Document

Upload or replace documents for an individual KYC application.

Use the `pending_documents` list from `POST /applications` or `GET /applications/{customer_id}` as the upload checklist. KYC2 document types are `ID_FRONT`, `ID_BACK` when applicable, and `SELFIE`; EDD uses `POA`.

Uploads are state-gated. ID/Selfie uploads are accepted in `DRAFT` and `ACTION_REQUIRED`. POA is accepted when EDD is in scope, when a Tier2-approved customer starts a proactive Tier3 upgrade, or as a pre-submit local-only upload in `DRAFT`. Re-uploading the same document type replaces the previous file.

Each file must be a base64 data URI (`image/jpeg`, `image/png`, or `application/pdf`) and must decode to **4 MB or less**. See the [Individual Onboarding Overview](https://developer.1money.com/reference/individual_onboarding_overview) for the document matrix and POA rules.

individual_applications.submit.description:
Submit Individual Application

Submit an individual application for asynchronous KYC2 evaluation.

Allowed when `kyc_status` is `DRAFT` or `ACTION_REQUIRED` and all KYC2 fields/documents are complete. The call returns `202 Accepted`, moves the application to `PROCESSING`, emits `kyc.submitted`, and starts ID/Selfie verification.

This endpoint is not resource-idempotent. An optional `Idempotency-Key` is used only for webhook correlation as `client_idempotency_key`; repeat calls after acceptance return a status conflict until the application moves to the next state.

Outcomes are delivered through KYC webhooks and can be reconciled with `GET /applications/{customer_id}`. See the [Individual Onboarding Overview](https://developer.1money.com/reference/individual_onboarding_overview) for outcome handling.

individual_applications.update.description:
Update Individual Application

Update an existing individual KYC application.

KYC2 profile groups (`contact`, `person`, `residential_address`, `document`) are editable while `kyc_status` is `DRAFT` or `ACTION_REQUIRED`. EDD fields (`due_diligence`) are editable while `edd_status` is `NOT_REQUIRED` or `REQUIRED`.

Nested objects are partial updates: omitted sub-fields keep their current value. Updating data does not restart verification by itself; call `POST /submit` for KYC2 or `POST /upgrade` for EDD when the required updates and documents are complete.

The response has the same metadata-only shape as `GET /applications/{customer_id}`. See the [Individual Onboarding Overview](https://developer.1money.com/reference/individual_onboarding_overview) for lifecycle rules.

individual_applications.upgrade.description:
Upgrade Account Tier

Trigger Tier3 / EDD evaluation for an individual application.

This endpoint accepts no request body. Before calling it, provide the required `due_diligence` fields with `PATCH /applications/{customer_id}` and upload `POA` with `PUT /applications/{customer_id}/documents`.

Allowed for the proactive Tier3 path (`kyc_status=APPROVED`, `edd_status=NOT_REQUIRED` or `REQUIRED`) and for KYC2-high recovery (`kyc_status=ACTION_REQUIRED`, `edd_status=REQUIRED`). The call returns `202 Accepted`, moves `edd_status` to `PENDING`, emits `kyc.upgrade_started`, and starts EDD evaluation.

The optional `Idempotency-Key` is webhook-correlation only. See the [Individual Onboarding Overview](https://developer.1money.com/reference/individual_onboarding_overview) for prerequisites, POA freshness, and EDD outcome webhooks.

individual_accounts.get.description:
Get Individual Account

Retrieve detailed information about an individual account.

## Prerequisites

The account must be in APPROVED status (KYC completed and approved). The `customer_id` (Customer ID) is returned during onboarding — once an application is approved, it becomes the account.

## Response Fields

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `customer_id` | Customer ID from onboarding |
| `email` | Account holder's email |
| `first_name` | Account holder's first name |
| `last_name` | Account holder's last name |
| `person` | Submitted personal information |
| `phone` | Submitted phone number |
| `address` | Submitted residential address |
| `identity` | Submitted identity information |
| `document` | Submitted identity document data |
| `due_diligence` | Submitted EDD data |
| `status` | Account status (`ACTIVE`, `SUSPENDED`, `CLOSED`) |
| `kyc_level` | `2` = Advanced KYC, `3` = EDD approved |
| `approved_at` | When the account was approved (RFC 3339) |
| `created_at` | When the application was created (RFC 3339) |

individual_accounts.get_limits.description:
Get Transaction Limits

Retrieve withdrawal limits for an individual account based on the current KYC level.

## Prerequisites

The account must be in APPROVED status.

## Limits by KYC Level

| KYC Level | Meaning | Limits |
|---|---|---|
| `1` | Basic KYC approved (US only) | Base daily + 30-day rolling limits |
| `2` | Advanced KYC approved | Standard daily + 30-day rolling limits |
| `3` | EDD approved | Highest daily + 30-day rolling limits |

## Response Fields

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `daily_withdrawal` | Maximum total withdrawal per calendar day (resets at UTC midnight) |
| `daily_withdrawal_used` | USD amount already withdrawn today (rounded to 2 dp) |
| `rolling_30d_withdrawal` | Maximum total withdrawal within a rolling 30-day sliding window |
| `rolling_30d_withdrawal_used` | USD amount already withdrawn in the past 30 days (rounded to 2 dp) |
| `currency` | Currency code for the limit amounts (e.g., `USD`) |

Get Deposit Instructions

Returns the default deposit instruction for a specified asset and network.

**Supported Instruction Types:**
- **Fiat** — Bank account details for Wire and SWIFT deposits
- **Crypto** — Wallet address for token deposits

**Default Wallet Addresses:**

Each customer is automatically assigned a default deposit address for the following networks:

| Network | Type |
|---|---|
| EVM (e.g. Ethereum, Polygon, BNB Chain) | Default wallet address |
| Solana | Default wallet address |
| Tron | Default wallet address |
| Bitcoin | Default wallet address |

Customers may also request additional deposit addresses on any of these networks. This endpoint always returns the default address only. To manage multiple addresses, use the following endpoints instead:

| Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|
| `GET /all_deposit_instructions` | List all deposit addresses across all networks |
| `POST /deposit_instruction` | Request an additional deposit address |
| `GET /deposit_instruction/{id}` | Retrieve a specific deposit address by ID |

> ⚠️ For crypto deposits, verify the token contract address carefully before transferring funds to ensure you are depositing the correct token.

auto_conversion_rules.create.description:
Create Auto-Conversion Rule

Create an Auto-Conversion Rule for fiat->crypto, crypto->fiat, or crypto->crypto conversions.

**Supported Assets:**
- `USD`, `USDC`, `USDT`, `PYUSD`, `RLUSD`, `USDG`, `USDP`, `EURC`, `MXNB`
**Supported Networks:**
- Fiat deposit networks: `US_FEDWIRE`, `SWIFT`
- Crypto networks: `ETHEREUM`, `POLYGON`, `BASE`, `ARBITRUM`, `AVALANCHE`, `BNBCHAIN`, `SOLANA`, `TRON`

**Validation Rules:**
- Supported pairs: fiat->crypto, crypto->fiat, and crypto->crypto; fiat->fiat is NOT supported
- `Idempotency-Key` header is required and must be a valid UUID v4
- Source network must match asset type (fiat asset requires fiat network, crypto asset requires crypto network)
- For crypto withdrawal destination: `network` is required when `wallet_address` is provided
- For fiat destination: `network` will be omitted

**Withdrawal Configuration:**
- Fiat-to-Crypto or Crypto->Crypto with withdrawal: provide `wallet_address` (external crypto wallet address)
- Crypto-to-Fiat with withdrawal: provide `external_account_id` (bank account ID from external-accounts API)
- Conversion-only (no withdrawal): omit both fields, converted funds remain in customer's account

**Idempotency & Webhook Behavior:**
- This endpoint creates resources asynchronously. The webhook notification may arrive **before** the HTTP response returns.
- Use the `Idempotency-Key` to query the resource status via webhook response, enabling proper idempotency control.
- **Recommended flow:** Instead of waiting for the HTTP response and then the webhook, clients can use the webhook arrival as the completion signal and query by `Idempotency-Key` to verify the result.
- This approach prevents "dangling wait" scenarios where clients unnecessarily wait for the HTTP response when the webhook has already confirmed the outcome.

**Response & Status:**
- The response will have `status=PENDING` and `source_deposit_info=null` because deposit info is being prepared asynchronously.
- Once deposit info is ready, the status will transition to `ACTIVE` and `source_deposit_info` will contain bank deposit details or crypto wallet address.
- Use the retrieve endpoint or webhook to get the full details when the rule becomes `ACTIVE`.

**Note:** List response does not include `source_deposit_info`. Use the retrieve endpoint to get full details including deposit info.

**Sub-accounts**
Set `include_subaccounts=true` on the main account to list Auto-Conversion Rules across the main account and all sub-accounts under the same enterprise. Sub-account requests are always scoped to that sub-account. Each item carries its owning `customer_id` and `account_id`. Defaults to `false` (current customer only).

**Pagination**
Two query parameter formats are supported:
- Flat format (recommended): `?page=1&size=10`
- Nested format: `?pagination=page=1&size=10`

List Auto-Conversion Orders

Retrieve the execution history (orders) for a specific Auto-Conversion Rule.

## Response Structure
Each order includes:
- Order metadata (ID, status, timestamps)
- Source and destination asset info
- Fee receipt breakdown
- **Sub-transactions array** (ordered: deposit → conversion → withdrawal)

## Sub-Transaction Types
- `DEPOSIT`: Initial fiat/crypto deposit
- `CONVERSION`: RFQ conversion (if applicable)

**AUTO_CONVERSION Response**
For AUTO_CONVERSION transactions, the response includes:
- Main transaction metadata (ID, status, source/destination assets)
- `sub_transactions` array with individual steps:
- `transaction_id`: Sub-transaction ID
- `transaction_action`: DEPOSIT | CONVERSION | WITHDRAWAL
- `status`: Current status of the sub-transaction
- `amount` / `asset`: Transaction amount and asset
- `to_amount` / `to_asset`: Target amount and asset (for conversion)
- `created_at`: Timestamp

**Note**:
For SWIFT withdrawals, UETR is populated in the reference field.

fees.estimate.description:
Estimate Transaction Fees

Get estimated fees before executing a transaction.

**Actions:**

- `DEPOSIT`: Deposit of assets
- `WITHDRAWAL`: Withdrawal of assets
- `CONVERSION`: **Not supported** - use `/conversions/quote` instead

**Fee Calculation:**

The fee is determined by combining `action` + `asset`:
- DEPOSIT + Crypto asset (USDC, USDT, etc.) → No fee
- DEPOSIT + Fiat currency (USD, EUR, MXN) → Fiat deposit fee
- WITHDRAWAL + Crypto asset → Crypto withdrawal fee (includes gas)
- WITHDRAWAL + Fiat currency → Fiat withdrawal fee

**Notes:**

- Crypto withdrawal fees include network gas fees and may fluctuate
- Fiat fees are fixed rate + percentage

**Networks:**

- Crypto: ETHEREUM, POLYGON, ARBITRUM, AVALANCHE, BASE, BNBCHAIN, SOLANA, TRON
- Fiat: US_ACH, US_FEDWIRE, US_RTP, SWIFT, CUBIX, BANK_TRANSFER, PIX_TRANSFER

partner_fees.create.description:
Create Partner Fee

Create a partner fee charged to your customers, under the given account.

**Scope:**

- Create on the **main account** to set a default fee that applies to all sub-accounts.
- Create on a **sub-account** to set a fee that applies only to that sub-account.

**Fee matching:** when a transaction occurs, a sub-account fee takes priority over the main-account default, and the most targeted fee wins.

**external_id:** required valid UUID in the request body, unique to this create request. Reusing an existing value returns a conflict. If a previous create timed out, look it up via the list endpoint with the `external_id` query parameter instead of replaying the create request.
